title: Number of Distinct Islands II
summary: Given an m x n binary matrix grid, where 1 represents land and the edges of the grid are surrounded by water, count the number of distinct island shapes.
statement: Given an m x n binary matrix grid, where 1 represents land and the edges of the grid are surrounded by water, count the number of distinct island shapes. Two islands are considered the same if one can be transformed into the other through rotations (by 90, 180, or 270 degrees) or reflections (over the vertical or horizontal axis).
constraints: Grid cells are zero or one and islands connect orthogonally.
Shapes are equivalent under translation, rotation, or reflection.
hints: A planar shape has eight rotation/reflection orientations.
Generate all signed coordinate swaps, translate each to the origin, and choose one canonical tuple.
Flood-fill cells; transform by swap/no-swap and both axis signs; normalize minima; take lexicographic minimum.
Equivalent shapes generate the same set of eight normalized orientations, so their minima match exactly.
editorial: Equivalent shapes generate the same set of eight normalized orientations, so their minima match exactly.
